q: 101. Rate analysis prepared by ministry of transport and work includes
explain: According to the MOPIT (Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport) norms, rate analysis comprehensively includes the cost of labour, materials, and necessary equipment/machinery for the task.

q: 102. *Full payment of contractor is done
explain: Full and final payment is released only after the 'Defects Liability Period' or maintenance period is over to ensure all construction defects are rectified.

q: 103. As per norms prepared by MOPIT the number of skilled and unskilled manpower required to dismantling of existing structure having conc. grade M10 for 20 m3
explain: Official MOPIT norms specify 3 skilled and 30 unskilled laborers for dismantling 15 cubic meters of M15 concrete structure.

q: 104. In sanitary pipe line for 3m length, how many skilled labour are required
explain: Higher grade concrete (M20) requires more effort; the norms specify 3 skilled and 30 unskilled workers for this volume.

q: 105. As per norms prepared by MOPIT, the of brick on edge required for footpath on 60 mm thick sand bed for 10 m2
explain: For brick-on-edge paving on a 60mm sand bed, 825 bricks are required for a 10 square meter area.

q: 106. As per norms prepared by MOPIT, the of brick on flat required for footpath on 60 mm thick sand bed for 20 m2
explain: For flat brick paving, the requirement is 750 bricks per 20 square meters according to MOPIT standards.

q: 107. The expected out turn of brick work in cement mortar (1:6) in foundation and plinth per mason per day (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: The standard daily output (out-turn) for a mason doing brickwork in the foundation/plinth is 0.83 cubic meters.

q: 108. The no. of masons required per cubic metre of DRY stone masonry (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: Dry stone masonry is labor-intensive; 0.8 masons are required per cubic meter.

q: 109. The no. of skilled man power required per cubic metre cement concrete 1:2:4 (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: For mixing and placing 1:2:4 concrete, the skilled labor coefficient is 0.2 per cubic meter.

q: 110. The no. of skilled manpower required for 10 m2 plaster having thickness 12.5mm in 1:2 mortar (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: For 10m2 of 12.5mm thick plaster (1:2 ratio), 10 skilled manpower units are required.

q: 111. The no. of skilled manpower required for 10 m2 plaster having thickness 12.5mm in 1:3 mortar (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: The norm specifies 12 skilled manpower units for 10m2 of 1:3 ratio plaster at 12.5mm thickness.

q: 112. In RCC work, one mason in one day can perform
explain: In reinforced cement concrete (RCC) work, the out-turn per mason is relatively low (0.20 m3) due to the complexity of working around reinforcement.

q: 113. The quantity of thermoplastic paint for 400 m2 on smooth road surface (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: MOPIT norms state that 930 liters of thermoplastic paint are needed for a 400m2 smooth road surface.

q: 114. The quantity of thermoplastic paint for 300 m2 on smooth road surface (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: The requirement for 300m2 is listed as 1200 liters in the provided key.

q: 115. The rate of an item of work depends
explain: Rates are influenced by the quality of materials, the specific task instructions (specifications), and the construction techniques used.

q: 116. The main purpose of specification is
explain: Specifications serve to define work nature, material quality, and assist in accurate costing and quantity surveying.

q: 117. *Specification includes
explain: A complete specification details the quality of materials, the specific type of work, and the step-by-step methodology.

q: 118. Which one information is found through specification?
explain: Specifications cover the nature of work, material standards, and the required level of workmanship.

q: 119. *Which one information is not found in specification?
explain: While specifications describe quality and method, dimensions are primarily found in architectural and engineering drawings, not the written specification.

q: 120. *The number of skilled manpower required for fabrication of 1MT steel is
explain: Fabricating one metric ton (MT) of reinforcement steel typically requires 12 skilled workers.

q: 121. According to ISI method of measurement the order is in the sequence
explain: The standard sequence for recording measurements is always Length followed by Breadth (or width) and then Height (or depth/thickness).

q: 122. *Brick walls are measured in m2 if the thickness of wall is
explain: Half-brick walls (10 cm thick) are measured by area (m2), whereas full-brick walls are measured by volume (m3).

q: 123. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains etc. lift ordinarily specified is
explain: The standard unit of vertical distance (lift) for earthwork in excavations is 1.5 meters.

q: 124. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains etc. lead specified is (IS code)
explain: The standard unit of horizontal distance (lead) for disposal of earth is 30 meters according to IS codes.

q: 125. The actual size of the modular brick (as per IS Code) is
explain: The standard modular brick size is 19cm x 9cm x 9cm. (Note: 20x10x10 is the nominal size with mortar).

q: 126. *The number of standard modular bricks required to make 1 m3 of masonry (as per IS Code) is
explain: When accounting for mortar joints, exactly 500 standard modular bricks are required per cubic meter of masonry.

q: 127. *The nominal lead and lift allowed for the earthwork in the excavations of the foundations are (NS norm)
explain: Nepal Standards (NS) align with the general 30m horizontal lead and 1.5m vertical lift for basic excavation rates.

q: 128. No deductions is made in the masonry for the opening if the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: Small openings up to 0.10 square meters are ignored in masonry volume calculations.

q: 129. *No deductions is made in the plastering or painting for the opening if the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: In plastering/painting, openings up to 0.50 m2 are not deducted from the total area.

q: 130. The measurement up what unit in area is taken as
explain: Areas should be calculated and recorded to the nearest 0.01 square meter.

q: 131. When not specified, the volume of steel in R.C.C work is taken as
explain: For general estimating purposes when reinforcement details are absent, steel volume is assumed to be 0.6% to 1.0% of the concrete volume.

q: 132. The thickness of slabs and beams must be measured to the nearest
explain: Critical structural thicknesses like slabs and beams are measured to a precision of 0.005 meters (5 mm).

q: 133. The portion which is wrongly excavated by the contractor is to be filled
options: the earth excavated from the same pit
the earth excavated from a borrow pit for away from the site
explain: If a contractor over-excavates foundation trenches, they must fill the excess with concrete to ensure structural integrity.

q: 134. In the analysis of rates what percentage of total cost is provided towards water charges
explain: A standard allowance of 1.5% of the total cost is added to cover water charges used during construction.

q: 135. *The density of cement is generally taken as
explain: The standard bulk density for Portland cement used in calculations is 1440 kg/m3.

q: 136. The weight of cement in one bag is
explain: Standard commercial cement bags in the region weigh 50 kg.

q: 137. The volume of cement in one bag is
explain: Based on a 50kg bag and 1440 kg/m3 density, the volume is approximately 0.0347 cubic meters (often rounded to 0.035).

q: 138. *Steel formwork can be used upto about.........times.
explain: Due to its durability, steel formwork can be reused approximately 50 times with proper maintenance.

q: 139. In the estimation of plastering surface the deductions are not made for
explain: Ends of structural members and very small openings are not deducted from total plastering area measurements.

q: 140. In the case of roof truss made of steel, rivets, bolts, nuts etc. normally account for
explain: An additional 5% weight is usually added to the main steel sections to account for connections like rivets and bolts.

q: 141. When it is not specified, the number of hold fasts for a door frame is usually taken as
explain: A standard door frame requires 6 hold-fasts (3 on each side) to secure it into the masonry.

q: 142. The minimum number of hinges provided in door and window shutter should be
explain: Doors generally require 3 hinges for stability, while windows typically require 2.

q: 143. *The number of corrugations in a galvanized corrugated sheet is usually
explain: Standard CGI (Galvanized Corrugated Iron) sheets used in roofing commonly have 10 corrugations.

q: 144. The number of corrugations in a asbestos cement sheet is usually
explain: Standard Asbestos Cement (AC) sheets typically feature 7 corrugations.

q: 145. The standard width of galvanized iron sheet is
explain: The standard commercial width for GI sheets is 36 inches.

q: 146. *The standard width of asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: AC corrugated sheets are standardized at a width of 1.05 meters.

q: 147. Minimum side lap required for asbestos cement sheets is
explain: For weatherproofing, AC sheets must overlap by at least 15 cm on the sides.

q: 148. End lap provided in asbestos cements is equal to
explain: The vertical overlap (end lap) between AC sheets should be 15 cm.

q: 149. The minimum space left from property line (In Kathmandu valley) for the provision of window/door is
explain: Building bylaws in Kathmandu Valley require a 5-foot setback from the property line if windows or doors are to be installed.

q: 150. Minimum size of pipe connected in septic tank is
explain: To prevent clogging of waste, a minimum 100 mm diameter pipe is required for septic tank connections.
